record.original_question: Give a mathematically meaningful characterization of what should count as an interesting or natural mathematical question.

evidence.quote: 2. What is an interesting or natural mathematical question? (G. J. Chaitin)

artifact.self_contained_problem: Provide a mathematically rigorous and meaningful characterization of the informal notion of an "interesting" or "natural" mathematical question. More precisely, propose a formal definition, criterion, or measure (for instance, in terms of algorithmic information theory, Kolmogorov complexity, logical depth, proof-theoretic strength, definability, or any other precise framework) that distinguishes those mathematical statements or problems which would intuitively be regarded as interesting or natural from those that would not, and justify that the proposed characterization captures the intended informal notion.
artifact.status_search_result: The question, posed by G. J. Chaitin, is a foundational/philosophical open problem in algorithmic information theory. No formal mathematical characterization of an "interesting" or "natural" question has been established; the problem remains open as of available sources.
